narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

instructor.rule: counts out loud; demonstrates front and back; three slow repetitions before tempo; one correction at a time

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Created in the late 1920s by Leonard Reed and Willie Bryant, the routine was originally called 'Goofus' and performed on the T.O.B.A. circuit.
It later became a staple in Harlem venues and was popularized as a line dance at the Savoy Ballroom.
on_screen: Map: United States · North America
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Originally a grand finale for stage shows, it is now a standard line dance at swing events, often serving as a transition into social Lindy Hop.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: File:Shim Sham at CCX 2022.webm (https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/93/Shim_Sham_at_CCX_2022.webm?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=original)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance consists of 10 phrases of choreography, each lasting four 8-counts.
It features four primary steps: the Double Shuffle, the Cross Over, Tack Annie, and Falling Off a Log, followed by a break.
Watch for Double Shuffle, Tack Annie, Falling Off a Log.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (268jUcVRdoY)
Captions name each signature move as it appears

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is performed to swing music, ideally with melodies starting on beat eight.
Common tracks include 'The Shim Sham Song' and 'Tain't What You Do (It's The Way That Cha Do It).'
Listen for the Brass, Rhythm section.
The pulse is 4/4.
Swing music with a steady pulse, often featuring breaks that align with the dance's choreographed pauses.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Leonard Reed, Willie Bryant, Frankie Manning, Al Minns, Leon James, Dean Collins.
Variations include the original 1927 version, the Freeze Chorus, the Joe Louis Shuffle, the Shim Sham II, and The Revenge of the Shim Sham.
Developed from tap dance routines on the T.O.B.A. circuit and adapted into a line dance by Lindy hoppers at the Savoy Ballroom.
